title: PM daily scratchpad 2026-03-17
body:
2026-03-17 PM scratchpad

Top priorities for today:
- Finalize PRD edits for Dedicated Burst Autoscale (see notes below). Need sign-off from SRE + infra.
- Sync w/ Applied ML about fallback model variant policy in burst (how to pick quantized vs full fp).
- Prepare canary rollout checklist + ops runbook for next Wednesday.
- Follow up on ENG-891 (autoscaler bug impacting min replicas on node drain).

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Update PRD section: failure mode & rollback criteria (Maya to review)
- [x] Draft canary metrics (latency p95, error rate, cost per token delta) - initial sent to Tom 3/16
- [ ] Add runbook step for manual scale-to-zero recovery
- [ ] Create short explainer for sales (1-pager) about burst capacity limits and SLAs

Meetings / timeboxed notes:
- 09:00 




— Standup (prod-dedicated): flagged ENG-891 as blocker for canary. SRE to triage ETA EOD.
- 10:30 



— PRD review w/ Maya & Priya (30m):
  - Need to clarify: burst_capacity defined as percentage of dedicated pool vs absolute GPU count. Recommend % for multi-tenant fairness.
  - Priya: prefer guardrail of max-burst-per-customer metric to avoid noisy neighbors. Add to constraints.
  - Action: Jordan to update PRD constraint section + add example config snippets (by EOD).
- 13:00 

— Sync applied-ml: discussed fallback model ordering when burst uses quantized variants. Key decision: prefer latency SLO first, then cost. Need to add policy table to PRD.
- 15:00 

— Ops + SRE: canary rollout sequencing + monitoring dashboards. Agreed p95 & error-rate alert thresholds, and automatic rollback if sustained >2x baseline error rate for 5m. Tom to own alerts.

PRD edits (notes to self):
- Add \"Failure modes\" subsection: capacity-exhaustion, cross-tenant noisy neighbor, model-variant quality regression, autoscaler flapping. List implications and rollback actions.
- Add example config JSON (2 snippets):
  1) conservative: max_burst_pct: 20, per_customer_max_gpus: 2
  2) aggressive: max_burst_pct: 50, per_customer_max_gpus: 8
- Add metrics for canary:
  - latency: p50/p90/p95/p99
  - correctness: sample eval set pass rate + user-level error signals
  - cost: tokens served and cost delta vs baseline
- Document canary window: 10k requests or 24 hours (whichever first), with automatic rollback rules.

Stakeholder follow-ups (who / what / when):
- Maya (PM lead) — review PRD constraints + examples (due 3/18)
- Tom (SRE) — triage ENG-891 and confirm alert thresholds (due EOD today)
- Priya (Applied ML) — provide recommended fallback ordering for model variants (deliver 3/18)
- Solutions Eng (Lena) — draft 1-pager for sales on burst behavior + SLAs (draft by 3/19)
- Legal/Compliance  — check on data residency implications for cross-region burst (cc: compliance@redwood).

Launch checklist (next Wednesday canary):
- Pre-launch:
  - [ ] Final PRD sign-off (Maya + Priya)
  - [ ] ENG-891 fixed or mitigation in place
  - [ ] Dashboards in Grafana + sigint alerts configured (Tom)
  - [ ] Runbook published to Confluence + link in pager duty event
  - [ ] Canary infra: ability to pin a subset of tenants and traffic routing rules tested
- During canary:
  - Rolling enable for 5% tenants -> 20% -> 50% over 4 hours windows
  - Monitor p95 latency, error rate, and cost delta; sample inference outputs for quality regression
  - Engage applied-ml for any quality anomalies
- Post-canary:
  - Postmortem doc if any incidents
  - Update PRD with lessons learned and adjust defaults if needed

Blockers / Risks:
- ENG-891 (autoscaler droops min replicas during node drain) — if unresolved, must disable aggressive burst and only run conservative configs.
- Model variant fallback quality unknown for some heavy context models; need applied-ml to provide quality gates.
- Sales expectations: customers expect burst to be transparent and instant — need clear limits in docs to avoid disappointment.

Notes / random thoughts:
- Could add an \"opt-in burst preview\" for early customers with higher quota + cost share. Helps surface edge cases.
- Consider default config templates in Console: \"Conservative\", \"Balanced\", \"Aggressive\". Makes onboarding easier.

Next actions for me (Jordan):
- Update PRD constraint + examples (EOD)
- Follow up with Tom on ENG-891 status at 11:30
- Draft the canary runbook skeleton and share with Ops by EOD

References / links:
- PRD (working): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PROD/pages/987654321/Dedicated+Burst+Autoscale+PRD
- Jira: DEDICATED-412, ENG-891
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1207

End of scratchpad.
